# About this project {.unnumbered}

[بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم]{.aralt}

Mortimer Sloper Howell
([Wikipedia entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortimer_Sloper_Howell))
published his
_A Grammar of the Classical Arabic Language_
from 1880--1911.

It has more than 4000 pages printed across 7 books.
The scanned PDFs are hosted at: <https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013>.

This [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) book aims to make
his work more navigable.

Here is a summary breakdown of the parts and sections into the individually bound books:

+ Volume 1 (Part\ 1, pp.\ 1--1813)
  + Book 1 (Part\ 1, Fasciculus\ 1):
    + Frontmatter
    + Introduction (§\ 1, pp.\ i--xliii)
    + Part\ 1: The noun (Chapters\ 1--4, §§\ 2--158, pp.\ 1--498)
    + Notes (pp.\ [1A--88A](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book1_1-498/page/n672/mode/2up))
  + Book 2 (Part\ 1, Fasciculus\ 2):
    + Part\ 1: The noun (Chapters\ 5--6, §§\ 159--233, pp.\ 499--861)
    + Notes (pp.\ [87A--134A](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book2_499-861/page/n397/mode/2up))
  + Book 3 (Part\ 1, Fasciculus\ 3):
    + Part 1: The noun (Chapters\ 7--11, §§\ 234--312, pp.\ 862--1422)
    + Notes (pp.\ [181A--189A](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book3_862-1422/page/n622/mode/2up))
  + Book 4 (Part\ 1, Fasciculus\ 4):
    + Part 1: The noun (Chapters\ 8--17, §§\ 313--401, pp.\ 1423--1813)
    + Notes (pp.\ [189A--223A](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book4_1423-1813/page/n434/mode/2up))
+ Volume 2 (Parts\ 2--4, pp.\ 1--1850)
  + Book 5 (Part\ 2 and Part\ 3):
    + Part 2: The verb (§§\ 402--496A, pp.\ 1--282)
    + Part 3: The particle (§§\ 497--624, pp.\ 283--735)
    + Notes (pp.\ [1A--30A](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book5_1-735/page/n344/mode/2up))
  + Book 6 (Part\ 4, Fasciculus\ 1):
    + Part 4: The common processes (Chapters\ 1--10, §§\ 625--730A, pp.\ 736--1622)
  + Book 7 (Part\ 4, Fasciculus\ 2):
    + Part 4: The common processes (Chapter 11, §§\ 731--759, pp.\ 1633--1850)
    + Appendix (pp.\ i--xxvii)
    + Notes (pp.\ [29A--181A](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book7_1663-1850/page/n216/mode/2up)
    + Index to references to the Quran (pp.\ [i--xxvii](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book7_1663-1850/page/n369/mode/2up))
    + Index of proper names (pp.\ [i--cxxxvi](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book7_1663-1850/page/n392/mode/2up))
    + Index of subjects (pp.\ [i--liii](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book7_1663-1850/page/n528/mode/2up))
    + Final additions and corrections (pp.\ [1--9](https://archive.org/details/howellarabicgrammar2013/howell-arabicgrammar-snap-book7_1663-1850/page/n581/mode/2up))

For links to the individual sections, I build upon the work done by
Aasim Iqbal
([جزاه الله خيرًا]{.ar}) published on his
[site](https://revivearabic.blogspot.com/2016/03/grammar-classical-arabic-language-howell-arabicgrammar-pdf.html)
and hosted at
<https://archive.org/details/AI2_reuploads2>.

For an interesting read on Howell's methodology vis-a-vis contemporary trends in the Western study of Arabic grammar, see:

+ Jean-Patrick Guillaume, "Deux grammaires de l’arabe à contre-courant: A Grammar of the Classical Arabic Language de M.\ S. Howell et la Grammaire arabe composée d’après les sources primitives de D.\ Vernier," in _Documenter et décrire les langues d'Asie: Histoire et épistémologie_. 
  <https://books.openedition.org/shesl/10369?lang=en>

Another interesting general read:

+ Carolyn G. Killean, "The development of western grammars of Arabic," _Journal of Near Eastern Studies_, vol.\ 43, no.\ 3, 1984. <https://doi.org/10.1086/373081>

## How to use this web-book

### Navigating

In order to use this web-book, first navigate to the chapter from the sidebar on the left.
It will open a chapter page with two frames:

1. The frame on the left is an embedded PDF of the combined table of contents (ToC).
2. The frame on the right either:
   a. Opens that chapter, if it has only one section. 
   b. Or it lists links to the sections contained in that chapter.
      Scroll through the ToC to determine your desired section number.
      And click on the link for your desired section number to open it in that frame.
      In order to go back to the clickable section list, click the back button on your browser.

### Linking to a specific page

In order to link to a specific page within a chapter, append `?page=` followed by the page number to the URL.
The page number is the one listed on the horizontal progress bar on archive.org.

For example: <https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/1-03-0.html?page=179>

This opens page\ 179 of Book\ 1 according to the numbering of archive.org
(which more-or-less corresponds to the page number of the PDF).
This happens to be printed page\ 6.

There is no bounds checking, so you'll have to make sure you're linking within the right chapter/book.

## Notes regarding the text

+ Numbers in square brackets in running text, for example "[402]", are a cross-reference to that section number.
+ Howell's own opinions are within brackets.
